claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared as a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution without deliberate precipitates or chemical short-range order.
The low hardness and strength of solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi are governed by intrinsically low resistance to dislocation motion.
The base CoCrFeNiTi alloy has only modest lattice distortion.
Modest lattice distortion and a lack of nanoscale obstacles produce low barriers for dislocation nucleation and glide.
Multiple slip systems activate with little resistance in the base CoCrFeNiTi alloy.
Easy dislocation motion promotes plasticity while reducing work hardening, hardness, and strength.
A minor addition such as approximately 0.1 at.% B can induce precipitates or local chemical ordering in CoCrFeNiTi.
A 0.1 at.% B addition can leave the underlying solid-solution matrix phase substantially unchanged while producing a secondary precipitate population.
Nanoscale precipitates or short-range ordered regions act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Introducing nanoscale obstacles raises the stress required for dislocation nucleation and glide.
Raising the stress required for dislocation motion increases yield strength and hardness.
Modified CoCrFeNiTi containing induced precipitates or ordering will have significantly greater yield strength and hardness than the starting alloy.
The modified alloy will show more dislocation obstruction and possibly different dislocation or twinning behavior than the base alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies in the single-phase, room-temperature regime under uniaxial loading.
Cryogenic temperatures or extremely high strain rates may activate additional mechanisms such as twinning and alter the strengthening response.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mediator require formation of precipitates, which creates a multiphase structural state, while the boundary states that the mechanism applies in a single-phase regime. This could be reconciled by explicitly defining the boundary as a single-phase matrix containing a small precipitate fraction.
